sites.siteName: Katherine River Corridor (greenfield screen — southern DKIS fringe)

matrix.reason: Available screen footprint is 200 ha against a 0.8 ha reactor envelope; land status: Crown land / pastoral lease — Jawoyn and Dagoman Aboriginal country; FPIC obligations; nuclear banned. Tenure, zoning, heritage and indigenous/title constraints still require confirmation.

Federal law is the dominant screen-level blocker: EPBC Act s.140A bars approval for construction/operation of a nuclear power plant and ARPANS Act s.10 bars ARPANSA licensing; the site therefore fails the nuclear licensing entry gate regardless of otherwise attractive physical attributes.
A nuclear project would trigger environmental assessment and public consultation; protected-area, habitat, discharge, cultural heritage and social acceptance issues require field-level review.

eVinci Microreactor is dry/air-cooled at screen level; the site cooling source is therefore not a primary siting constraint, though heat rejection and local thermal design must be confirmed. Site cooling note: Katherine River — seasonal tropical river; highly variable flow (wet: abundant, dry: minimal); not reliable for continuous cooling
Grid distance is 0 km. Existing switchyard/grid proximity lowers friction where present; longer distances or isolated/off-grid contexts require new interconnection/load studies.

Population density is marked low and hazards include flood-high, heat-extreme, seismic-low. EPZ, exclusion-area control, security standoff and severe-weather/geotechnical assumptions require project-specific analysis.

Screen logistics are inferred from industrial/port/brownfield status, road/rail/grid proximity and available laydown footprint; oversize transport routes, port handling and construction laydown need route survey.

regionSummary: Northern Territory has physically attractive sites for the selected reactor, but Australia has a dominant federal statutory prohibition: EPBC Act s.140A prevents approval for nuclear power plant construction/operation [au-epbc-140a], and ARPANS Act s.10 prevents ARPANSA from issuing the required licence [au-arpans-10]. The screen therefore marks every candidate as fail on Gate B, even where land, cooling, grid or logistics appear favourable.
